title: Rav Yehudah of Hagronia
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman says he is mentioned once, in [Avodah Zarah 39a](https://www.sefaria.org/Avodah_Zarah.39a.15): Chanan the tailor bought tekhelet (blue dye) from the members of the household of Rabbanai, the brother of Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba. He came before Rav Matna, who did not have [a ruling] at hand. He came before Rav Yehudah of Hagronia, who said to him, "You have fallen into my hand" ("now you need me," [Rashi](https://www.sefaria.org/Rashi_on_Avodah_Zarah.39a.15.1)). Rav Yehudah then cited Shmuel. Hyman says Yuchasin omitted this notice, while [Yuchasin HaShalem](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yohasin-zakut/yohasin-zakut08.pdf#page=47) mentions it under "Chanan." Hyman considers it more likely to follow the reading of R-G, that Chanan came before Rav Yehudah (the student of Shmuel) and [he] said to him, "From Hagronia it fell into [my] hand." See there.[^1][^2][^3]

notes.text: Hyman prefers the reading in which “from Hagronia” belongs to the speech. He cites it under the initials ר״ג. The alternative leaves the speaker and the possessor of “hand” implicit. The source Hyman denotes by ר״ג remains unidentified.

The linked Bavli calls him Rav Yehudah of Hagronia and reads “you have fallen into my hand.” Rashi explains, “Now you need me.” [Heilprin’s brief notice](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1719&lang=en) gives the encounter in a different direction from the Bavli.

The 1857 [Yuchasin HaShalem, p. 143](https://www.daat.ac.il/daat/vl/yohasin-zakut/yohasin-zakut08.pdf#page=47) names Rav Yehudah of Hagronia under Chanan the tailor and gives his ruling on the wife of a chaver. [Rabbeinu Chananel](https://www.sefaria.org/Rabbeinu_Chananel_on_Avodah_Zarah.39a.13) also puts the disputed word inside the speech. He reads “you have fallen” and takes the word to mean “a quarrelsome man.” Hyman’s preferred version instead says “it fell.”
